lines.line: A man got 18 months for having bots play his AI songs.
lines.frame0: PRISON FOR HAVING BOTS PLAY HIS SONGS
lines.emotion: Surprise, then a moral itch: 'prison, for that? Who did he even hurt?' Robots playing a man's own songs sounds victimless, so a normal viewer has to find out who got robbed, and a real, recent sentence makes it instantly believable.
lines.backing: FL 1.8 (its own safe wording), 4.9 (18 months, sentenced 2026-10-06), 4.10 (prosecutors: hundreds of thousands of AI songs, billions of bot plays, paid for years), 3.1-3.3 and 3.7 (the shared pot); pair any harm claim with 4.14-4.15 and 8.6 (contested: never 'stole $8M from artists'); 7.10 (no AI tool named).
lines.payoff: It answers 'who did he rob?': streaming doesn't pay per play, each month's money is a shared pot split by share of all plays, so every bot play that got past the filters was paid out of the same pot as every real artist, a sliver from each.

lines.line: A song can get paid without a single real listener.
lines.frame0: PAID WITHOUT A SINGLE REAL LISTENER
lines.emotion: Disbelief with a sting of unfairness: everyone assumes you get paid when people listen, and real musicians fight for every listener, so a song earning with nobody real listening breaks the most basic rule and begs 'how, and whose money?'
lines.backing: FL 4.10, 4.12 (bot accounts playing AI songs, paid for years before the charges), 2.4-2.5 (one app: up to 85% of AI-track plays fake in 2025, fake plays the main reason they're uploaded), 3.1-3.3, 3.7 (the pot split by share of plays), 4.1-4.2, 8.2 ('can': caught fakes earn nothing, some slip through).
lines.payoff: Bots do the listening, and since each month's money is a shared pot split by share of all plays, a fake play that slips past the filters takes its slice from the same pot that pays every real artist, leaving each of them a little less, by an amount nobody has measured.

lines.line: Bots can shrink your favorite artist's paycheck.
lines.frame0: BOTS CAN SHRINK YOUR FAVORITE ARTIST'S PAYCHECK
lines.emotion: Protective indignation plus a 'how?': nearly everyone has a favorite artist they want paid fairly, and robots reaching that pay without touching their songs sounds impossible, so the viewer stays for the trick; the 'you' is natural because the loss is the artist's, never the viewer's.
lines.backing: FL 3.2-3.3, 3.7 (Spotify: 'as total streams grow, you need more streams to maintain the same share'), 7.4 (Spotify: spam 'can dilute the royalty pool'), 6.4 (Apple: 'This is a zero-sum game'), 4.1-4.2, 8.2 ('can': only uncaught fakes), 8.1 and 7.6 (size unmeasured, Deezer calls it 'minimal on Deezer': the payoff says 'a little'), 3.6 ('paycheck' is fair shorthand).
lines.payoff: The bots never need to touch your artist's songs: each month's money is a shared pot split by share of all plays, so every fake play that slips past the filters makes every real slice a little thinner, your artist's included, by an amount nobody has measured.

lines.line: Your subscription gets split with songs you've never heard.
lines.frame0: SONGS YOU'VE NEVER HEARD SHARE YOUR FEE
lines.emotion: Personal surprise and a small sting: people assume their monthly fee goes to the artists they play, so learning it's pooled with songs they've never heard feels like finding out your tip went into one jar for the whole street; the 'you' is natural because it is literally their money.
lines.backing: FL 3.3 (the pot is that market's subscription and ad money), 3.2 (split by share of all plays), 3.11 (safe wording: 'Your monthly fee goes into the shared pot, not just to the artists you play'), 3.6; the bot half qualified per 4.1-4.2 and 8.2 (never 'your subscription pays for AI songs').
lines.payoff: The loop closes on its own words: some of those songs no human has heard at all, only bots, and while most of those fake plays get caught and stripped out, the ones that slip through take a slice of the same shared pot your fee went into, leaving every real artist you play a little less.

lines.line: Who pays when a bot plays an AI song?
lines.frame0: WHO PAYS WHEN BOTS PLAY AI SONGS?
lines.emotion: Curiosity with a whiff of unfairness: it sounds like a riddle with a real answer; most people would guess 'the app pays', so the hint that someone else covers a robot's 'listening' itches until it's answered.
lines.backing: FL 3.1-3.3 (no per-play rate; a shared pot per country per month, split by share of plays), 3.7, 6.4 ('This is a zero-sum game'), 4.1-4.2 and 3.13 (caught fakes stripped out: the honest 'nobody' half), 8.1-8.2 (the uncaught share is unmeasured), 2.4, 4.10 (bots playing AI songs is real); 4.3, 4.5 (bots play human songs too: never imply it's only AI).
lines.payoff: The answer has two halves: if the filters catch it, nobody, because caught fakes are stripped out of the pot; if it slips through, every real artist in that month's shared pot pays a sliver, by an amount nobody has measured.

lines.line: Why would anyone make songs just for bots?
lines.frame0: WHY MAKE SONGS JUST FOR BOTS?
lines.emotion: Bafflement that turns into suspicion: songs with an audience of robots sound absurd and a bit eerie, a normal person can't think of a reason, and the only answer that fits, money, raises the real question: whose money?
lines.backing: FL 2.5 (one app: fake streams are 'the main purpose for uploading AI-generated music'), 4.10-4.11 (Smith's email: 'a TON of content with small amounts of Streams'), 2.3-2.4, 3.1-3.3, 3.7, 4.1-4.2, 8.2; 5.13, 6.12 (say that plenty of AI-using artists want real fans: fraud, not AI).
lines.payoff: Because streaming doesn't pay per play: each month's money is a shared pot split by share of all plays, so a song nobody wants plus fake plays that slip past the filters can pull a real slice out of the same pot that pays every real artist.

lines.line: One streaming app found most plays on AI songs were fake.
lines.frame0: ONE APP: MOST AI-SONG PLAYS WERE FAKE
lines.emotion: Shock and suspicion: a play count is something everyone trusts at a glance, so hearing that most plays on AI songs were fake makes a normal person ask who fakes plays, and why that would ever pay.
lines.backing: FL 2.4 ('up to 85% of these streams were fraudulent in 2025, depending on the month'), section 9 step 2 ('most of the plays they do get are fake', on Deezer's numbers only), 8.4 (say 'one app'; small 'Deezer, 2025' credit on frame 0), 2.5, 4.2, 3.1-3.3; 4.3 and the Never-say list: the problem is fake plays, not AI songs.
lines.payoff: It answers 'why fake the plays?': each month's money is a shared pot split by share of all plays, so a faked play is a claim on real money; that app caught and stripped out the fakes it found, but any that slip past the filters take their slice from every real artist in the pot.

lines.line: Bots want a slice of Spotify's $11 billion payout.
lines.frame0: BOTS WANT A SLICE OF $11 BILLION
lines.emotion: Heist intrigue: a huge, concrete pile of money from an app everyone uses, and robots trying to sneak a piece of it; a normal person wonders how a robot could get paid at all, and whose share it comes out of.
lines.backing: FL 3.4 ('Spotify paid out $11 billion last year'), 3.1-3.3 (no per-play rate; split by share of plays, per country per month: never 'one pot'), 3.7, 6.4, 4.1 and 7.1 (Spotify doesn't pay for fakes it catches: give it credit), 4.10, 4.15 (fakes have got through before), 8.1-8.2.
lines.payoff: There's no per-play rate: each month, in each country, that money is a shared pot split by share of all plays, so any fake play that slips past the filters takes its slice out of the same payout as every real artist, a sliver from each.
